# OidFed

> OidFed is an Apache-2.0 OpenID Federation SDK for JavaScript and TypeScript. Use it to run a Trust Anchor, an Intermediate, or a Leaf, verify trust chains and Trust Marks, or add federation trust to OIDC, OAuth, and digital wallet applications.

## Start here

- [Documentation](https://oidfed.com/docs): Feature guides, example code, package API reference, and migration instructions.
- [TypeScript quickstart](https://oidfed.com/#quickstart): Create a Trust Anchor, an Intermediate, or a Leaf. A fourth example composes an OIDC Relying Party and a wallet Credential Verifier on one Leaf.
- [Choose a federation host](https://oidfed.com/docs/features/1.1.entity-roles): Create a host, attach protocol roles, and enroll participants with their immediate superior.
- [OIDC and OAuth workflows](https://oidfed.com/docs/features/15.oidc-and-oauth): OpenID Providers and Relying Parties, OAuth clients, authorization servers, and protected resources. Use automatic or explicit client registration with your protocol engine.
- [Wallet workflows](https://oidfed.com/docs/features/16.wallet): Wallet Providers, Credential Issuers, and Credential Verifiers. Establish trust, verify Wallet Attestations, and prepare or check presentation requests with the application's credential engine.

Construct federation hosts with `TrustAnchor.create()`, `Intermediate.create()`, or `Leaf.create()`. Attach roles in `roles`, serve federation routes with the host's `handleRequest(Request)`, and use Core directly when you only need trust discovery and verification. Your application provides HTTPS serving, crypto, signing custody, storage, and its OIDC, OAuth or wallet protocol engine.

OidFed implements [OpenID Federation 1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-1_1-final.html) and the [OpenID Connect 1.1 profile](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-connect-1_1-final.html). The six libraries use Web APIs and share a test suite across Node.js, Deno, Bun, workerd, Electron, and Chromium.

## Packages

- [@oidfed/crypto](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/crypto): Crypto engine and signer contracts, signing keyrings and compact JWS utilities. Includes Web Crypto and optional JOSE adapters.
- [@oidfed/core](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/core): Entity Statements, trust-chain discovery and validation, metadata policy, Trust Marks, Entity Collection, and the shared storage contract.
- [@oidfed/authority](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/authority): Trust Anchor and Intermediate Authority operations: subordinate management, statement issuance, and federation endpoint handlers, including fetch, list, resolve, Extended Listing, Subordinate Events, and Entity Collection.
- [@oidfed/leaf](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/leaf): Leaf Entity toolkit — Entity Configuration serving, authority discovery, and trust chain participation for any entity at the edge of a federation (typically RPs or OPs that don't issue subordinate statements).
- [@oidfed/oidc](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/oidc): OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 federation flows — automatic and explicit client registration, Request Object validation, and typed RP/OP metadata processing as defined in OpenID Federation 1.0 §12.
- [@oidfed/wallet](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/wallet): Wallet Provider, Credential Issuer, and Credential Verifier roles, federation trust checks, JWT Wallet Attestations, and protocol-engine integrations.

## Tools

- [@oidfed/cli](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/tools/cli/docs/readme.md): Command-line interface for inspecting, validating, and debugging OpenID Federation deployments: resolve trust chains, decode entity statements, verify signatures, check trust mark status, generate keys, sign statements, and query listing, collection, and event endpoints. Install with `npm i -g @oidfed/cli`.

## Apps

- [@oidfed/home](https://oidfed.com): Library quickstart, ecosystem, and Trust Journal. Machine-readable overview: <https://oidfed.com/llms.txt>.
- [@oidfed/explorer](https://explore.oidfed.com): Visual federation-exploration tool — inspect entity configurations, trace trust chains, browse metadata, validate topology. Browser-based, no backend. Machine-readable overview: <https://explore.oidfed.com/llms.txt>.
- [@oidfed/learn](https://learn.oidfed.com): Interactive OpenID Federation 1.0 course — 15 lessons from first principles to federation topology design. Machine-readable overview: <https://learn.oidfed.com/llms.txt>.

## Documentation

- [Trust Journal](https://oidfed.com/trust-journal) collects standards updates, guides, deployment reports, and related digital trust resources.
- [v3 Migration](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/migration-v3) covers dependency, crypto, storage, and public API changes.
- [React Native Compatibility](https://oidfed.com/docs/api/react-native) covers Metro, URL parsing, and streaming HTTP setup for mobile apps using Core or Wallet.
- [Wiring Guide](https://oidfed.com/docs/features/11.5.http-wiring): End-to-end integration with Express.js and `panva/node-oidc-provider`. Worked eduGAIN-topology example covering Trust Anchor, Intermediate, OP, and RP.
- [Storage Guide](https://oidfed.com/docs/features/11.6.storage-adapters): Configure one storage adapter for subordinate records, events, Trust Marks, collection snapshots, replay protection, and caching.
- [SECURITY](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Vulnerability disclosure policy.

## Related Specifications

- [OpenID Federation 1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-1_1-final.html) *(Final)* covers the protocol-independent trust framework.
- [OpenID Federation for OpenID Connect 1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-connect-1_1-final.html) *(Final)* covers the OpenID Connect and OAuth bindings. [OpenID Federation 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-1_0.html) covers both layers in one specification.
- [Extended Subordinate Listing 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-extended-listing-1_0-ID1.html) *(Implementer’s Draft 1)* adds paginated listings, audit timestamps, and selected Subordinate Statement claims. OidFed provides server, client, and CLI support.
- [Subordinate Events 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-subordinate-events-1_0-ID1.html) *(Implementer’s Draft 1)* defines signed authority histories. OidFed supports transactional event recording and verified retrieval.
- [Entity Collection Endpoint 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-entity-collection-1_0-01.html) *(Draft 01 implemented)* covers filterable discovery of direct and indirect subordinates. [Draft 02](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-entity-collection-1_0-02.html) is a separate standards update.
- [Wallet Architectures 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-wallet-1_0-05.html) *(Draft 05 implemented)* covers federation trust for Wallet Providers, Credential Issuers, and Credential Verifiers. Applications supply their OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP engines. [Draft 06](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-wallet-1_0-06.html) adds federation processing for Verifier Attestations.
- [ACME with OpenID Federation 1.0](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-acme-openid-federation/) *(Expired Internet-Draft)* proposed using federation to establish trust in certificate issuance.

## Federation Operator Notes

Running a federation involves responsibilities beyond what this library enforces. Operators must read and address OpenID Federation 1.0 §17 (Implementation Considerations — multi-path ambiguity, Trust Mark policy design, resolver/TA co-location), §18 (Security Considerations — DoS prevention, `authority_hints` depth limits, Trust Mark filtering, reverse-proxy end-to-end signing), and §19 (Privacy Considerations — minimising personal data, short-lived Trust Mark Status tokens). This library provides the protocol mechanisms; policy, rate limiting, key management, HSM integration, and operational hardening are the operator's responsibility.

## Security

Report vulnerabilities to <dah.kenangnon@gmail.com> — see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for the full disclosure policy. Do not open public GitHub issues for security reports.
